item.title: Hogansville approves 90-day moratorium for data centers
item.description: Hogansville imposes 90-day halt on all data center proposals, including plans for the Hightower Road sprayfield site, as officials rework regulations and table a new heavy industrial zoning district.

item.title: CONTRIBUTOR'S VIEW - Bill King: The Lunch Box Museum
item.description: A Columbus, Georgia collector's 5,000-lunchbox hobby became the world-famous Lunch Box Museum, now part of seven small museums discovered by a visiting cigar-box instrument maker.

item.title: Development Authority approves funding for new Downtown LaGrange master plan
item.description: LaGrange Development Authority OKs shared funding for first new downtown master plan in 25 years, expanding focus to nearby neighborhoods and LaGrange College connections.

item.title: CONTRIBUTOR'S VIEW - Richard Ingram: Explaining Lafayette: Lafayette and Tolstoy
item.description: Richard Ingram explores how Lafayette and Tolstoy—born generations apart—illuminate Tolstoy’s “two stories” and “hedgehog and fox” ideas, casting Lafayette as a single-minded hedgehog.

item.title: Two men shot, one killed, on Big Springs Mountville Road
item.description: Man killed, another wounded in Big Springs Mountville Road shooting; suspect arrested and charged with murder after reported dispute.

item.title: Troup freshman qualifies for state swim meet for first time
item.description: Braxton Ralph is ready for state. The Troup High freshman is the school’s lone state qualifier in swimming for the 2025-26 season. The youngster will be diving into the deep end on Thursday at the Georgia Tech Aquatic Center. Thursday’s state meet will be unlike anything Ralph has experienced before. item.title: Black History Program to again celebrate students
item.description: West Point’s 23rd annual Black History Program returns Feb. 24, honoring local students and community groups with performances and a talk by “$1.00 Thursday Man” Anthony Talley.

item.title: Troup rallies for bounce-back win
item.description: Sheniyah Philpot’s 20-point surge powers Troup’s second-half rally in a 47-37 win over larger East Coweta, giving the Tigers a key bounce-back victory after their 11-game streak ended.
